title: AnchorPoint Craft — onboarding sprint notebook
content:
AnchorPoint Craft — onboarding sprint notebook (personal scratchpad)

Purpose: capture raw notes from kickoff, technical constraints, quick hypotheses for cost/latency, and concrete next steps. NOT a polished handoff — internal memory for SE/sprint.

-- Call log: 2026-03-10 10:00 PST (kickoff) --
Attendees: Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood Solutions Eng), Anya (Redwood PM), Elena Park (AnchorPoint CTO), Samir Patel (AP infra lead), Ravi Chopra (AP SRE)
Key asks from AnchorPoint:
  - Replace heuristic product-recommendation microservice with LLM-backed reranker for checkout upsell (goal: +2.5% AOV).
  - Must run in their VPC (private deployment) with no customer data leaving network.
  - 99.9% availability during US peak hours. P95 latency target for end-to-end inference <= 300ms; p50 < 120ms.
  - Support for streaming partial results to frontend (progressive rank scores) so they can display intermediate suggestions.
  - HSM for key storage (YubiHSM) and mTLS for control-plane auth.

Initial technical notes (raw):
  - AP stack: Ruby GraphQL API -> sidecar worker pool (Sidekiq) -> SQS for bursts -> recommendation worker calls Redwood private endpoint.
  - Typical request size: 1–4 candidate items (avg tokens per candidate prompt ~ 120 tokens). Expected 200–350 RPS at peak with big holiday spikes to 900 RPS for 10–15 minutes. Bursty pattern (cron promotions + ads).
  - On-device caching already exists for product metadata but not for model responses. Opportunity: prefix caching for product descriptions + user cart history.

Constraints and gotchas observed on call:
  - No egress allowed from VPC (customer policy). Must deploy Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane or use Dedicated with VPC peering + strict egress ACLs. Confirm which is viable.
  - HSM integration: AnchorPoint insists on customer-owned KMS/HSM. Private deploy needs KMS integration guide — check Private docs for HSM connectors (PKCS#11 support).
  - Legal: log retention limit 30 days and aggregated telemetry only — must disable token-level logging in pilot config.
  - Frontend requires SSE/streaming; Redwood runtime supports streaming but need to route via internal LB and ensure HTTP/2 support in their sidecar. Also their GraphQL layer strips chunked responses by default — SRE must change behavior.
  - Quantization: customer willing to accept slight quality delta for cost savings. But product ranking is sensitive to tiny score differences — will require eval set.

Quick perf hypotheses (for sprint):
  - Baseline: 1x LLM (non-quantized) pinned to GPU A100-nl (single model) -> expected p95 server-side latency ~ 120–180ms for 120-token prompt w/ small KV cache hit rate. End-to-end p95 likely ~ 250–350ms depending on network.
  - Target config: 8-bit quantized variant + prefix KV cache + dynamic batching limit 16 -> expected token cost cut 2.2x and p95 latency stable <= 300ms under 400 RPS.
  - Fallback plan: model-splitting into smaller reranker model (distilled) for degraded mode to preserve availability under extreme bursts.

Immediate checklist (what to validate this week):
  - [ ] Confirm AnchorPoint legal OK with data plane config: confirm whether payloads may be temporarily stored for caching (they said no persistent storage).
  - [ ] Engineering: get sample payloads and a small representative eval set (200 queries) to measure quality delta after quantization/distillation. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2026-03-15.
  - [ ] Infra: validate VPC peering approach vs Private air-gapped installer. Need decision: VPC peering with strict ACLs (faster) OR Private deployment (longer lead). Owner: Samir + Priya. Due: 2026-03-13.
  - [ ] Security: confirm HSM integration path (vendor model + connector). Owner: Anya. Due: 2026-03-14.
  - [ ] Product: define metrics dashboard: p50/p95 latency by route, token cost per request, top-case accuracy degradation (A/B on sample eval set). Owner: Anya. Due: 2026-03-17.

Short runbook sketch (pilot):
  1) Day 0–2: environment prep — VPC peering, firewall rules, service account + mTLS cert exchange. No model traffic.
  2) Day 3–4: smoke tests using a tiny subset of traffic (10 rps). Verify streaming, auth, KMS calls.
  3) Day 5–7: run eval harness (200 queries) comparing baseline model -> quantized -> distilled reranker. Produce quality delta table.
  4) Day 8–14: ramp to 100–400 rps with autoscaling policy. Monitor p95 and token cost; enable fallback model routing if p95 exceeds 500ms.

Prompt engineering notes (scratch):
  - Prompt template used by AP: "You are a product recommender. Given cart items (list), candidate items (list). Score candidates 0..1 and return JSON array of {id,score,reason}. Keep reasons <= 20 words."
  - Danger: anchors in reason text leak business rules — redact internal PII. Add system instruction to remove PHI.
  - Quick sample prompt (for eval harness):
      SYSTEM: "Assistant provides a numeric relevance score for each candidate and terse rationale. Output ONLY valid JSON array."
      USER: "Cart: [SKU: A123 (red shirt), SKU: C555 (jeans)] Candidates: [B222 (belt), D999 (hat), E101 (socks)]"

Experiment ideas (to capture):
  - Re-ranking with hybrid signal: combine model score * 0.7 + business boost * 0.3 (business boost deterministic). Evaluate lift.
  - Local distilled fallback model for cold start: run distilled model in CPU instance (<50ms inference) for very short bursts, then async re-rank with full model for quality logging.

Risks flagged:
  - Quality regressions from quantization may drop conversion. Must gate behind A/B on eval set.
  - GraphQL + SSE mismatch is the most immediate engineering blocker.
  - HSM/KMS procurement could add 3–4 weeks if customer insists on on-prem HSM network setup.

Open questions to triage (send in follow-up email):
  - Elena: exact KMS/HSM vendor and whether PKCS#11 interface is available.
  - Ravi: can GraphQL gateway be configured to accept chunked SSE responses? Listing the exact NGINX/Sidekiq version would help.
  - Samir: do they have a dedicated subnet for workloads that will be allowed to reach Redwood nodes (if peering)? Any firewall partner rules?

Next steps (concrete):
  - Priya to draft 1-page deployment options doc comparing VPC peering vs Private deploy with timelines (send by 2026-03-12).
  - Marcus to request sample eval set & product metadata JSON schema from AnchorPoint (due 2026-03-15).
  - Schedule a follow-up demo of streaming from Redwood Private in their VPC (target week of 2026-03-22). Owner: Priya + Marcus.
  - Create a minimal RBAC matrix for pilot (who in AP can see token-level logs) — to be minimal per legal. Owner: Anya.

Random engineering shorthand / scratch commands (for my memory):
  - Example curl (dev-only):
    curl -X POST https://private-infer.anchorpoint/v1/generate \
      -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model":"anchorpoint-reranker-v1","input":"<prompt>","stream":true}'

  - Suggested runtime config snippet (pseudo):
    model: anchorpoint-reranker-v1
    quantization: int8_dynamic
    batch_window_ms: 12
    max_batch_size: 16
    kv_prefix_cache: true

Notes-to-self: keep this doc alive until pilot is stable (remove internal TODOs and produce crisp pilot-run playbook). Move final runbook to Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-2453/pilot-runbooks/anchorpoint.

End of scratchpad.
